Jordan / Marissa,

We need to raise an urgent reliability concern that is now affecting our renewal conversation. Over the last six weeks we've seen intermittent tail-latency spikes on inference for our credit-decisioning flow. The spikes are small in absolute time (100-300ms), but for our synchronous path they cause retries and downstream queuing that increase error rates.

This has caused three customer-facing incidents in the last month. Our ops team has instrumented traces and pointed to burst behavior during peak windows. We appreciate the support your team provided during the incidents, but the pattern is recurring and our leadership is asking for a concrete remediation that can be contractually bound for the renewal.

We are evaluating two things: (1) a firm SLA uplift or addendum that includes a tail-latency SLO and (2) a short-term priority-reserve (burst) pilot that guarantees capacity during our peaks while we migrate to a more resilient async path. If we cannot get a clear operational remedy and contractual guardrails by the end of September, our renewal will be delayed while we validate alternatives.

Can you propose a viable technical + commercial path this week? We are available for a 30 min call on Wednesday morning PT.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos

- Provisioning: if we use ephemeral priority hosts (logical reserve on existing pool with preemption), we can stand up the policy in ~6 business days. If FinHorizon wants guaranteed physical hosts (Dedicated nodes), provisioning is ~18–22 business days and requires a committed minimum.
